incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager duty alert — gpu-host-io-errors triggered for inference-us-west1 pool. 15% 5xx over 2m, latency spikes. Runbook: <link>
pagerduty-bot: Paging oncall @ryan — Sev2. Incident channel: #incidents. Please acknowledge.
oncall-ryan: ack — I’m on it. grabbing logs and checking node health. assigning temporary priority to customer-facing endpoints.
infra-alyssa: I’m ssh-ing into gpu-host-17 (10.128.45.17) now. seeing repeated host disconn from nv-host-agent. ping flaky.
ryan-oncall: noted. triggering autoscale to spin up from fallback pool to shed load off inference-us-west1.
sre-samir: quick ask — any recent kernel updates on that host? could be regression. also check ECC counters.
infra-alyssa: running quick checks:
```
ssh gpu-host-17 sudo dmesg | tail -n 40
[ 12345.678901] pcieport 0000:00:01.0: AER: multiple Uncorr_Severity=Corrected
[ 12345.679012] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1e): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 12346.000000] kernel: GPU reset detected by watchdog
[ 12346.100000] ecc: error count incr on GPU 0: 42 -> 78
```
infra-alyssa: nvidia-smi shows GPU 0 in Unknown state, ECC counts climbed quickly.
eng-julia: customer impact — support console shows ~8% of requests returned 5xx in last 5m, concentrated in us-west1. no direct billing spikes. customers affected: 12 active API keys, top 3 heavy users seeing retries.
support-martin: contacting Tier 2 for impacted customers, issuing proactive message to those 3. drafting short status note.
ryan-oncall: immediate mitigations — cordon + drain gpu-host-17, failover traffic to inference-us-west1-fallback pool, increase concurrency cap on fallback to avoid overload.
infra-alyssa: cordoned and started drain. `kubectl drain gpu-host-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — pods migrating. provider shows host reboot loop in console (reboot at 2025-11-03T14:02:10Z, kernel panic earlier at 14:01:56Z).
ops-bot: Automated action: reroute policy applied -> inference-us-west1 now sending 60% traffic to fallback pool.
sre-samir: building timeline so far:
- 14:00:42 UTC: A spike in 5xx observed on inference-us-west1
- 14:01:10 UTC: Pager triggered (gpu-host-io-errors)
- 14:01:56 UTC: host kernel reported GPU reset / watchdog
- 14:02:10 UTC: provider-initiated reboot (visible in cloud console)
- 14:03:00 UTC: pods started failing healthchecks as they reconnect to GPU
- 14:04:30 UTC: cordon+drain started, fallback routing engaged
- 14:07:55 UTC: customer impact reduced to <1%

eng-julia: attaching sample logs from failed request (sanitized):
```
{"request_id":"r-abc123","model":"redwood-7b","error":"cuda: unknown error: device lost","latency_ms":1200}
```
sre-samir: initial hypotheses (ranked):
1) GPU memory ECC spike causing device resets -> host reboots (evidence: ECC counter jump in dmesg)
2) PCIe link flapping / AER corrected errors accumulating -> GPU falls off the bus
3) Noisy neighbor (other tenant heavy GPU ops) triggering host watchdog timeouts
4) Provider host firmware/kernel bug (less likely but possible given rapid reboots)

infra-alyssa: more logs from provider agent show repeated "watchdog: hardware watchdog triggered" and firmware WDT events. opening ticket with provider with logs + host id.
ops-bot: Created ticket CLOUD-INC-5012 with provider; attached dmesg, nvidia-smi dump, timestamps, ECC counts.
ryan-oncall: mitigation plan while root cause investigated:
- keep gpu-host-17 drained and in maintenance for now
- replace workloads onto dedicated fallback pool and scale extra nodes in fallback
- schedule all remaining hosts in that rack for increased monitoring (ECC > 10 triggers alert)
- if other hosts show similar pattern, start rolling drain

sre-samir: run these checks if you land on a host:
```
# ECC summary
nvidia-smi -q | grep -i "Ecc Mode" -A3
# PCIe errors
sudo dmesg | grep -i pcie
# check host logs
journalctl -u nv-host-agent -S "2025-11-03T13:50:00" | tail -n 200
```
eng-julia: customer comms: posting short notice to status with details and mitigation steps. ETA: update in 30m. linking status page: <status.redwood.example/incident/1765432100>
support-martin: sent targeted emails to top 3 customers. included mitigation (retries) and offer to assist with request routing.
infra-alyssa: provider response (ticket update): "We see host watchdog resets, firmware team investigating, recommend reprovisioning or migrating to a fresh host. No hardware replacement scheduled yet." asked for ECC card swap logs.
ryan-oncall: decision — reprovision node and rebuild host from image, keep it out of autoscaling pool until provider confirms hardware health. If reprovision fails, we will retire host permanently and mark for deeper postmortem.
sre-samir: logging hypotheses/actions in incident tracker. assigning follow-ups:
- @infra-alyssa open support case with host serial + attach ECC counters (action: CLOUD-INC-5012)
- @eng-julia coordinate customer status updates (action: STATUS-1765432100)
- @support-martin follow up with affected customers (action: CS-1765432100)
- @ryan-oncall run post-incident RCA scheduled for tomorrow 10:00 UTC (action: RCA-1765432100)

eng-julia: small note — we saw no increased latency on embeddings endpoints (different pools). suggests noisy neighbor is local to this host not broader network.
sre-samir: agree. next steps: collect core dumps, full dmesg, nv-host-agent logs, firmware WDT traces, and provider-supplied host telemetry. also check for co-tenants with high ECC or runaway GPU kernels.
infra-alyssa: host reprovision started. keeping node in maintenance. will paste reprovision logs here.
ops-bot: routing reverted to normal after fallback autoscale stabilized. current error rate <0.5% for inference-us-west1. continuing monitoring.
oncall-ryan: handing off to post-incident team. if anyone sees recurrence, re-open pager. thanks everyone for quick actions. :thumbsup:
